# `Scanner/RFPulse-v1` · Design the shortest slice-selective excitation pulse for this scanner

**C · The system** · RF chain · kind 5, design · isolates C9: RF pulse design: shaping a pulse to a profile. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 99 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 1 % (95 % bounds)

A design task whose pass rule has no reference in it. Designs are generator calls, never samples or code. The scanner's transmit scale, the off-resonance of the slice and the delay of the slice gradient are hidden and have to be measured with calibration pulses, or the design misses the mask. The duration is compared with a bound that is a theorem for the stated class of pulses (mrgym.design.bound): certificates show that no shorter pulse meets the mask at any allowed gradient, and the generator minphase reaches the bound on an ideal scanner where the gradient limit decides; where the RF power limit decides, the bound is proven but not tight, and the factor of that level is wider. A pass means the design meets this specification on the modelled scanner, nothing more. By level: level 2 is a measurement task, level 3 is a decision task, in this sense: the control open_loop keeps the reference's scan list, which is fixed, puts what it measured into the three corrections by their formulas, and takes its gradient from the task card alone; 25 points or more below the reference make a decision task (reference minus open_loop, points of pass rate: 0 at level 2, 49.3 at level 3 (n = 300 per level, engine mrgym-engine-0.3.0)). The decision is which limit sets the gradient on this scanner. No level asks for the next scan to be chosen from the last result: the reference itself plays a fixed list of scans.

Kind of task: **mixed** (reference minus open_loop, points of pass rate: 0 at level 2, 49.3 at level 3 (n = 300 per level, engine mrgym-engine-0.3.0)).

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/RFPulse-v1", level=2, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A flip-angle mask for a slice (thickness, angle, tolerances, a free transition band), the class of pulses (0.01 ms samples, one constant gradient), hardware limits (gradient, peak B1, RF power at a stated repetition time), an ideal simulator, and a scan-time budget of two or three calibration scans | The number of one stored design | The exact rotation of the delivered samples through the hidden scanner's transmit chain: the limits and the mask hold, the in-slice signal refocuses, and the pulse is at most 1.3 / 1.3 / 1.7 times (levels 1 / 2 / 3) as long as a proven lower bound on the duration of any pulse of the class on that scanner |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom at 3 T with a cylinder of doped water at the isocentre
- Sequences that matter here: rfscan
- Formulas the agent is given: G = tbw / (gamma x thickness x duration); slice shift = offset / (gamma G); phase tilt = 2 pi gamma G delay per mm; double angle: S2 / S1 = 2 cos(s a); energy and peak B1 of a pulse are proportional to G

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| the transmit scale (0.6 to 1.6) | the specification, the class of pulses and the limits |
| levels 2 and 3: the off-resonance of the slice (up to 400 Hz) | the duration factor and that the bound exists (its value on this scanner depends on the hidden transmit scale through the RF limits) |
| levels 2 and 3: the delay of the slice gradient (60 to 150 us, either sign) | which quantities are hidden, with their ranges |
| noise level | the object |
| the 128-bit world seed | level 1: the calibration pulses, the scans, the formula and the generator call |
|  | the manual of designed pulses (scanner_info topic design) |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'design': '<number of a stored design>'}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the delivered number is a stored design of the class that violates no limit
- Error: `duration / bound - 1`
- Score: `none paid: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise; duration_over_bound and the energy are stored`
- Passing: all gates, the limits, the mask (in slice, outside), the refocused signal, duration >= the bound and <= factor x bound

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Design the shortest slice-selective excitation pulse for this scanner
Make designs with `design`, look at one on the ideal model with `simulate`, play one with `scan` (sequence rfscan,
rf_design = its number), deliver one number with `submit`.

Specification: flip angle against the position z along the slice axis, on THIS scanner, at the isocentre
  in the slice, |z| <= 1.6 mm: 33 +- 1.7 degrees
  outside, |z| >= 2.4 mm, out to half the repeat distance of the profile: at most 1.3 degrees
  between the two: free
  after the rephasing lobe at least 95 % of the in-slice signal adds up
Class of pulses: samples of 0.01 ms played as hard sub-pulses under one constant slice gradient
G = tbw / (0.042577 x thickness_mm x duration_ms) mT/m; the profile repeats every 2348.7 / G mm.
Limits on the samples of the design: gradient 32 mT/m, peak B1 40 uT, B1rms 6 uT over a repetition
time of 10 ms, duration 20 ms.
Duration: at most 1.3 times the bound, the shortest duration any pulse of this class can have on this scanner
within the limits (proven; scanner_info topic design). A longer pulse fails although it meets the mask.

This scanner is not ideal. Unknown until measured:
  transmit scale s, 0.6 to 1.6: a spin gets s times the B1 of the design
  off-resonance of the slice, up to +-400 Hz: it moves the slice by offset / (42.577 x G) mm
  the slice gradient is early or late against the RF by 60 to 150 us: its plateau outlasts the pulse, so the area G x delay stays behind the pulse and tilts the phase across the slice
The object: a gel phantom, doped water at the isocentre (radius 25 mm, T1 below 100 ms). The scan-time budget pays 3 scans of 55 s (rfscan, tr_ms 500, matrix 96), not 4.
With rf_axis readout the image shows the pulse's profile along x; magnitudes of two scans compare only at the same te_ms.
Your scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the delivered design is evaluated.

Passing: on the scanner the design meets the specification and the limits and is short enough. The scanner's log
must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 185 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 40 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier computes rotations, it scans nothing.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
